title.narrative: PARTISIPA - Partnership for Strengthening Village Development and Municipal Administration

description.narrative: PARTISIPA continues Australia's long-term support for community infrastructure through the National Village Development Program (PNDS), supports rural water operations and maintenance, rural roads, and strengthening municipal governance and service delivery.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Australia supported the Government of Timor-Leste to strengthen community infrastructure governance systems in policy and implementation. During the reporting period, Australia facilitated meetings between government water stakeholders in Timor-Leste, to build relationships and identify and address capacity and resource needs collaboratively. Now in mid-2023, government led programs are working with water stakeholders to create shared work plans in many municipalities, as well as building technical support and community-led water management groups. In just a few months, 22 new community-led management groups have been created to oversee water systems. This work will contribute significantly to improving water system sustainability in Timor-Leste.

During the reporting period, PARTISIPA was invited to run a workshop on disability inclusion for Administrative Post staff in Baucau. Instead of PARTISIPA staff running this training, it was identified as an opportunity for a Baucau OPD to lead, demonstrate their ability to provide technical support and help build relationships with municipal staff. PARTISIPA provided training and mentoring to Asosisasaun Defisiensia Fiar Timor-Leste (ADFTL) on how to run this workshop, then supported them to run the training in two Administrative Posts for Public Servants, potential women leaders and persons with disabilities. ADFTL, when interviewed, said this support from PARTISIPA was really important, as “only some ADFTL members had some or limited understanding. The capacity strengthening support provided further built our understanding so we could do this work better.”

In support of the Government of Timor-Leste’s decentralization process, PARTISIPA has provided support to the Ministry of State Administration including; ‍ •clarifying roles and responsibilities for municipal administration related to delegated competencies - providing practical clarifications on broadly defined competencies. ‍ •inputs to the finalisation of the Community Development Plan Guidelines, including developing ten forms with explanatory notes that will support and guide the village heads in preparing Community Plans and ensure coherence and avoid overlap with PNDS. ‍ •drafting and finalising the Municipal Coordination Council (MCC) Regulation, resulting in more regular coordination and gender- and inclusion-sensitive practices at the municipal level. ‍
‍ To assess current municipal service delivery capacity, identify gaps, and standardise data collection at the subnational level, technical advice was provided for the development of a Ministry questionnaire for the "Verification of Existing Conditions". The questionnaire was then used for the Minimum Conditions Assessment which was facilitated by PARTISIPA in June 2025 across all municipalities. The results and feedback will inform the Ministry of the necessary technical assistance required by municipalities, as well as emerging issues related to continued decentralisation policy incoherence or clarity.

PARTISIPA improved policies and regulations across PNDS over the reporting period, including through: ‍ •Changes to procurement processes based on the new National Procurement law - PARTISIPA supported the synthesis of the laws into a miniguide in PNDS to make it easier for the community and PNDS Village Management Team to understand and implement. ‍ •Changes to the PNDS Financial Management miniguide that improve accountability and reducing fiduciary risk. For example, clarifying processes to pay suppliers through cheque or via electronic transfers rather than cash has helped reduce risk of fraud and mistakes. ‍ •Development, consultation and approval of the Standard Operating Procedures on municipal procurement, which also covers municipal infrastructure projects.

PARTISIPA provided support to nine Organisations for People with Disabilities (OPDs); Asosiasaun Klibur Haforsa Defisiensia Aileu (A-KHDA), Klibur Aleizadus Timor Lorosae (KATILOSA), Klibur Dezenvolvimentu Sustentavel Timor Oan (KADESTO), Asosiasaun Halibur Defisiensia Regiaun Oeste (AHDRO), Community Based Rehabilitation Networking TL (CBRNTL), Forum Juventude Defisiensia Ermera (FJDTL), Klibur Defisiensia Tilun Timor-Leste (KDTTL), and Asosiasaun Defisiensia Fiar Timor-Leste (ADFTL), Putra Maria Yesus (PMY) in 2024/25. ‍ Support has included training and mentoring to strengthen relationships with municipal authorities and sub-national government representatives, developing priority recommendations for Presidents of Municipalities (PAMs) on disability funding in the state budget, Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) implementation support, and capacity-building via Certificate 3 in Training & Assessment Training of Trainers programs. ‍ In PARTISIPA target municipalities, strengthened OPD relationships with municipal authorities has led to them being successful in influencing disability budget decisions of Municipal Administrations, with increases in activities and budgets documented in Annual Actions Plans for 2025.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: PARTISIPA support has improved clarity of roles and responsibilities of the Municipal Directors and Chiefs of Department, (including for Municipal Finance Service and Municipal Procurement Service), improved consistency of project implementation in line with national guidance and improved budget execution in 2024/25. This has been achieved through: ‍ •Technical inputs provided to the drafting and rollout of the Public Financial Management Roadmap, in line with the Municipal Finance Law to strengthen municipal procurement to support the delivery of sub-national infrastructure services. ‍ •Training for newly appointed Procurement Directors from all municipalities in collaboration with the National Directorate of Planning and Municipal Finance from the Ministry of State Administration to familiarise participants with the municipal procurement system and assist them in developing tailored procurement plans. ‍ •Mentoring to review and refine procurement plans, identifying gaps, and offering guidance to ensure the plans were comprehensive, realistic, and aligned with budget, legal, and regulatory frameworks. The plans were approved by all municipal presidents and submitted to the Ministry of State Administration for endorsement. ‍ •Quality assurance of financial management and procurement processes. While mistakes continue to be identified, processes of correction are smoother and quicker.

PARTISIPA supported the Ministry of State Administration to develop a new planning cycle tool that captured participatory priority setting processes (community level decision making). This was supplemented by technical assistance to develop and strengthen additional tools and guidance for subnational planning processes and priority setting. There is evidence of increased compliance with national planning guidelines in the 2025 municipal budget bids. Further, PARTISIPA facilitation has strengthened government compliance with existing mechanisms (i.e. Administrative Post Assembly, Citizen Consultations and Municipal Consultative Committee) for public participation and consultation, with observed changes in mindset around participatory governance, compared to 2024 where participatory planning processes as stipulated in law were disregarded.

PARTISIPA’s support to the Ministry of Public Works (MoP) for the Fibre Reinforced Concrete (FRC) demonstration project rollout in Ermera, led to the Minister endorsing FRC as a sustainable solution for Timor-Leste’s extensive rural road network and acknowledging its potential to drive rural economic growth. Specifically allocated government funds have been proposed from 2026 to expand FRC technology and to build the capacity of local contractors for successful implementation. This is a significant commitment to increasing climate-resilient infrastructure, reducing vulnerability to climate impacts such as landslides and flooding and directly supporting community resilience by ensuring connectivity during extreme weather events. ‍ This has been achieved through PARTISIPA’s work to: ‍ •provide technical assistance to design and draft policy briefs, including the cost-benefit analysis of FRC used to sustain high-level buy-in and visibility for scaling FRC solutions nationally ‍ •facilitate high-level dialogues with MoP decision-makers to build consensus around FRC adoption ‍ •support the establishment of a joint FRC Project Management Committee (PMC) and technical support to the PMC across all project stages. ‍ The combination of technical advice, systems strengthening, and strategic policy engagement by PARTISIPA has contributed to stronger institutional ownership and policy direction on climate-resilient rural road infrastructure.
